newsitem.title: FRANCE: French diplomacy on hold in election run-up.
newsitem.headline: French diplomacy on hold in election run-up.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette has put off trips to the United States and Germany because of a snap election on May 25-June 1 and a Franco-German summit has been postponed, the ministry said on Thursday.

Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said de Charette had postponed until soon after the election an official visit to Washington scheduled for April 29-30 after discussing it with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

"Since there is only one official visit a year to Washington, it appeared sensible to put off the visit until just after the election period. Madeleine Albright perfectly understood the postponement," he told a news briefing.

Rummelhardt said de Charette and Albright had a lengthy telephone conversation on Wednesday night. Paris and Washington are at odds over France's demands that the United States hand over NATO's Naples-based southern command to a European.
The spokesman said de Charette and his German colleague Klaus Kinkel had agreed to postpone a Franco-German ministerial meeting scheduled in Hamburg next Monday.
Diplomatic sources said a regular six-monthly Franco-German summit would be rescheduled from June 3 in the central French town of Poitiers.
President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who meet roughly every six weeks, last met in Bonn on April 9 and are due to meet again in Paris on May 20.
The snap election called by Chirac on Monday has also forced him to drop a planned stopover in Hong Kong during his May 15-18 visit to China.
